original_question: For virtual 3-manifolds defined from framed virtual link diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves, do virtual Kirby equivalence and classical Kirby equivalence coincide on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed classical links; what is the correct geometric-topology interpretation of a virtual 3-manifold; and does the alternative construction by surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization produce the same theory?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 5, "Virtual 3-manifolds," with supporting context from Section 4 (definition of a virtual 3-manifold) and Section 2.2 (stabilization for links in thickened surfaces). ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact three-part focus: virtual 3-manifolds as formal equivalence classes of framed virtual diagrams modulo generalized Kirby moves; the comparison between virtual Kirby equivalence and classical Kirby equivalence on ordinary 3-manifolds presented by surgery on framed links; and the proposed alternative construction via surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R up to stabilization. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
missing_details: The paper phrases the first subquestion as a comparison of two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds arising from this viewpoint: homeomorphism versus virtual equivalence; it then restates this by asking whether framed links K and L that are equivalent under virtual Kirby calculus must already be equivalent under classical Kirby calculus. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

It is implicit that K and L are surgery presentations of ordinary 3-manifolds by framed classical links, whereas a "virtual 3-manifold" itself is defined in Section 4 as a Kirby equivalence class of framed virtual links. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

For the surface-based alternative theory, the paper's nearby topological language shows what "up to stabilization" means in this context: isotopy in the thickened surfaces, homeomorphisms of the surfaces, and addition or subtraction of empty handles. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

The second subquestion is not just asking for intuition; it asks for an interpretation of these equivalence classes specifically "in the domain of geometric topology." ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))

No algebraic side conditions occur here: there is no ambient ring or field, no degree or homogeneity hypothesis, no nilpotency condition, and no asymptotic quantifier such as "for all sufficiently large m"; the relevant hidden assumptions are entirely topological. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
refined_question: In the Kauffman-Dye theory of virtual 3-manifolds, where a virtual 3-manifold is a Kirby equivalence class of framed virtual links, do the two equivalence relations on ordinary 3-manifolds coming from this viewpoint coincide: namely, if framed classical links K and L present ordinary 3-manifolds by surgery and K and L are equivalent under the virtual Kirby calculus, must they already be equivalent under the classical Kirby calculus? In the same setting, what geometric-topology object is represented by these virtual Kirby-equivalence classes, and does the alternative theory obtained by performing surgery on links in thickened surfaces S_g x R, taken up to stabilization, coincide with the Kauffman-Dye theory? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
equivalent_formulation: Do the two equivalences for ordinary 3-manifolds arising from this theory—homeomorphism and virtual equivalence—coincide? ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
justification: The draft is targeting the official open problem in Section 7, Problem 5, rather than a broader neighboring issue. Section 4 supplies the operative definition of a virtual 3-manifold as a Kirby equivalence class of framed virtual links, and Section 7, Problem 5 then asks exactly the three questions your draft paraphrases: whether virtual Kirby equivalence collapses to classical Kirby equivalence on ordinary 3-manifolds, what geometric-topology interpretation these classes have, and whether a stabilization-based surgery theory on links in S_g x R agrees with the Kauffman-Dye theory. Section 2.2 is the relevant nearby source for the meaning of stabilization in thickened surfaces. ([impan.pl](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/89015))
